verses.original: Μὴ κρίνετε ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε
verses.transliteration: Mē krinete hina mē krithēte
verses.literal: [Do] not judge or . . . you will be judged

verses.original: γὰρ ἐν ᾧ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: gar en hō krimati krinete krithēsesthe kai en hō metrō metreite metrēthēsetai hymin
verses.literal: For with the same judgment you pronounce you will be judged and with the measure you [use] it will be measured to you

verses.original: δὲ Τί βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ τοῦ σου ἀδελφοῦ ὀφθαλμῷ τὴν δὲ οὐ κατανοεῖς δοκὸν ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ
verses.transliteration: de Ti blepeis to karphos to en tō tou sou adelphou ophthalmō tēn de ou katanoeis dokon en tō sō ophthalmō
verses.literal: - Why do you look at the speck - in - - your brother’s eye - but fail to notice [the] beam in - your [own] eye

verses.original: ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ σου ἀδελφῷ Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ σου ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν σοῦ τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ
verses.transliteration: ē pōs ereis tō sou adelphō Aphes ekbalō to karphos ek tou sou ophthalmou kai idou hē dokos en sou tō ophthalmō
verses.literal: - How can you say to your brother Let me take the speck out of - your eye while [there is still] - a beam in your [own] eye

verses.original: ὑποκριτά πρῶτον ἔκβαλε τὴν δοκόν ἐκ τοῦ σοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ τοῦ σου ἀδελφοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ
verses.transliteration: hypokrita prōton ekbale tēn dokon ek tou sou ophthalmou kai tote diablepseis ekbalein to karphos ek tou tou sou adelphou ophthalmou
verses.literal: You hypocrite First take the beam out of - your [own] eye and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from - - your brother’s eye

verses.original: Μὴ δῶτε τοῖς κυσίν τὸ ἅγιον μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς ὑμῶν μαργαρίτας ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων ποτε μή‿ καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς αὐτῶν ποσὶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: Mē dōte tois kysin to hagion mēde balēte tous hymōn margaritas emprosthen tōn choirōn pote mē katapatēsousin autous en tois autōn posin kai straphentes rhēxōsin hymas
verses.literal: {Do} not give - dogs what is holy {do} not throw - your pearls before - swine If you do . . . they may trample them under - their feet and then turn [and] tear you to pieces . . .

verses.original: Αἰτεῖτε καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν ζητεῖτε καὶ εὑρήσετε κρούετε καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: Aiteite kai dothēsetai hymin zēteite kai heurēsete krouete kai anoigēsetai hymin
verses.literal: Ask and it will be given to you seek and you will find knock and [the door] will be opened to you

verses.original: γὰρ πᾶς ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται
verses.transliteration: gar pas ho aitōn lambanei kai ho zētōn heuriskei kai tō krouonti anoigēsetai
verses.literal: For everyone - who asks receives - he who seeks finds and to him who knocks [the door] will be opened

verses.original: Ἢ τίς ἄνθρωπος ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ὃν ὁ αὐτοῦ υἱὸς αἰτήσει ἄρτον ἐπιδώσει μὴ αὐτῷ λίθον
verses.transliteration: Ē tis anthrōpos estin ex hymōn hon ho autou huios aitēsei arton epidōsei mē autō lithon
verses.literal: - Which . . . - of you if his . . . . . . son asks for bread will give . . . him a stone

verses.original: ἢ καὶ αἰτήσει ἰχθὺν ἐπιδώσει μὴ αὐτῷ ὄφιν
verses.transliteration: ē kai aitēsei ichthyn epidōsei mē autō ophin
verses.literal: Or [if] he asks for a fish will give . . . him a snake

verses.original: οὖν εἰ ὑμεῖς ὄντες πονηροὶ οἴδατε διδόναι ἀγαθὰ δόματα τοῖς ὑμῶν τέκνοις πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ ὑμῶν Πατὴρ ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: oun ei hymeis ontes ponēroi oidate didonai agatha domata tois hymōn teknois posō mallon ho hymōn Patēr ho en tois ouranois dōsei agatha tois aitousin auton
verses.literal: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children how much more {will} your Father - in - heaven give good things to those who ask Him

verses.original: Πάντα ὅσα ἐὰν οὖν ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς οὕτως καὶ θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι ὑμῖν γάρ οὗτος ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται
verses.transliteration: Panta hosa ean oun hymeis poieite autois houtōs kai thelēte hina poiōsin hoi anthrōpoi hymin gar houtos estin ho nomos kai hoi prophētai
verses.literal: In everything . . . . . . then - do to others as . . . you would have - them do . . . . . . to you For this is [the essence of] the Law and the Prophets

verses.original: Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης ὅτι πλατεῖα ἡ πύλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι δι’ αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: Eiselthate dia tēs stenēs pylēs hoti plateia hē pylē kai eurychōros hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn apōleian kai polloi eisin hoi eiserchomenoi di’ autēs
verses.literal: Enter through the narrow gate For wide [is] the gate and broad [is] the way that leads to - destruction and many - - enter through it

verses.original: ὅτι στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: hoti stenē hē pylē kai tethlimmenē hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn zōēn kai oligoi eisin hoi heuriskontes autēn
verses.literal: But small [is] the gate and narrow the way that leads to - life and only a few - - find it

verses.original: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν προβάτων ἐνδύμασιν δέ ἔσωθεν εἰσιν ἅρπαγες λύκοι
verses.transliteration: Prosechete apo tōn pseudoprophētōn hoitines erchontai pros hymas en probatōn endymasin de esōthen eisin harpages lykoi
verses.literal: Beware of - false prophets [They] come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly they are ravenous wolves

verses.original: ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν καρπῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς μήτι συλλέγουσιν σταφυλὰς ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν ἢ σῦκα ἀπὸ τριβόλων
verses.transliteration: apo tōn autōn karpōn epignōsesthe autous mēti syllegousin staphylas apo akanthōn ē syka apo tribolōn
verses.literal: By - their fruit you will recognize them - Are grapes gathered . . . from thornbushes or figs from thistles

verses.original: οὕτως πᾶν ἀγαθὸν δένδρον ποιεῖ καλοὺς καρποὺς τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον ποιεῖ πονηροὺς καρποὺς
verses.transliteration: houtōs pan agathon dendron poiei kalous karpous to de sapron dendron poiei ponērous karpous
verses.literal: Likewise every good tree bears good fruit - but a bad tree bears bad fruit

verses.original: ἀγαθὸν δένδρον δύναται οὐ ποιεῖν πονηροὺς καρποὺς σαπρὸν δένδρον οὐδὲ ποιεῖν καλοὺς καρποὺς
verses.transliteration: agathon dendron dynatai ou poiein ponērous karpous sapron dendron oude poiein kalous karpous
verses.literal: [A] good tree cannot . . . bear bad fruit [and a] bad tree cannot bear good fruit

verses.original: πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καλὸν καρπὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ βάλλεται εἰς πῦρ
verses.transliteration: pan dendron mē poioun kalon karpon ekkoptetai kai balletai eis pyr
verses.literal: Every tree vvv that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into [the] fire

verses.original: ἄρα¦γε ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν καρπῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: ara¦ge apo tōn autōn karpōn epignōsesthe autous
verses.literal: So then by - their fruit you will recognize them

verses.original: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι Κύριε Κύριε εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀλλ’ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ μου Πατρός τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς
verses.transliteration: Ou pas ho legōn moi Kyrie Kyrie eiseleusetai eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn all’ ho poiōn to thelēma tou mou Patros tou en tois ouranois
verses.literal: Not everyone who says to Me Lord Lord will enter . . . the kingdom of heaven but only he who does the will - of My Father - in - heaven

verses.original: πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ Κύριε Κύριε ἐπροφητεύσαμεν οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐξεβάλομεν δαιμόνια καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐποιήσαμεν πολλὰς δυνάμεις
verses.transliteration: polloi erousin moi en ekeinē tē hēmera Kyrie Kyrie eprophēteusamen ou tō sō onomati kai tō sō onomati exebalomen daimonia kai tō sō onomati epoiēsamen pollas dynameis
verses.literal: Many will say to Me on that - day Lord Lord did we not prophesy . . . in Your name and [in] Your name drive out demons and - - - perform many miracles

verses.original: καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι ἔγνων Οὐδέποτε ὑμᾶς ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν
verses.transliteration: kai tote homologēsō autois hoti egnōn Oudepote hymas apochōreite ap’ emou hoi ergazomenoi tēn anomian
verses.literal: - Then I will tell them plainly . . . - I never knew . . . you depart from Me [you] workers - of lawlessness

verses.original: οὖν Πᾶς ὅστις ἀκούει τούτους τοὺς λόγους μου καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς ὁμοιωθήσεται φρονίμῳ ἀνδρὶ ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν
verses.transliteration: oun Pas hostis akouei toutous tous logous mou kai poiei autous homoiōthēsetai phronimō andri hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn petran
verses.literal: Therefore everyone who hears these - words of Mine and acts on them is like [a] wise man who built his - house on the rock

verses.original: καὶ ἡ βροχὴ κατέβη καὶ οἱ ποταμοὶ ἦλθον καὶ οἱ ἄνεμοι ἔπνευσαν καὶ προσέπεσαν ἐκείνῃ τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ ἔπεσεν οὐκ γὰρ τεθεμελίωτο ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν
verses.transliteration: kai hē brochē katebē kai hoi potamoi ēlthon kai hoi anemoi epneusan kai prosepesan ekeinē tē oikia kai epesen ouk gar tethemeliōto epi tēn petran
verses.literal: - The rain fell - the torrents raged and the winds blew and beat against that - house yet it did not fall . . . because its foundation was on the rock

verses.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων τούτους τοὺς λόγους μου καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται μωρῷ ἀνδρὶ ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον
verses.transliteration: kai pas ho akouōn toutous tous logous mou kai mē poiōn autous homoiōthēsetai mōrō andri hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn ammon
verses.literal: But everyone who hears these - words of Mine and vvv does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his - house on - sand

verses.original: καὶ ἡ βροχὴ κατέβη καὶ οἱ ποταμοὶ ἦλθον καὶ οἱ ἄνεμοι ἔπνευσαν καὶ προσέκοψαν ἐκείνῃ τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ ἔπεσεν καὶ μεγάλη ἦν ἡ αὐτῆς πτῶσις
verses.transliteration: kai hē brochē katebē kai hoi potamoi ēlthon kai hoi anemoi epneusan kai prosekopsan ekeinē tē oikia kai epesen kai megalē ēn hē autēs ptōsis
verses.literal: - The rain fell - the torrents raged and the winds blew and beat against that - house and it fell and great was - its collapse

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐτέλεσεν τοὺς λόγους τούτους οἱ ὄχλοι ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ αὐτοῦ διδαχῇ
verses.transliteration: Kai egeneto hote ho Iēsous etelesen tous logous toutous hoi ochloi exeplēssonto epi tē autou didachē
verses.literal: - vvv When - Jesus had finished - saying these things the crowds were astonished at - His teaching

verses.original: γὰρ ἦν διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἔχων ἐξουσίαν καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ αὐτῶν γραμματεῖς
verses.transliteration: gar ēn didaskōn autous hōs echōn exousian kai ouch hōs hoi autōn grammateis
verses.literal: because He taught - as [one] who had authority and not as - their scribes
